title: Low flow — centrifugal pump differential diagnosis
applicability: Centrifugal pump with identifiable installed pump curve and known speed/impeller configuration
Liquid service; exact fluid and system arrangement must be captured
Not a substitute for OEM instructions or site operating procedures
mechanism: Low measured flow is an operating-point symptom, not a root cause. The operating point depends on the pump curve and system resistance; low speed, suction-side restriction, discharge/system restriction, internal wear, gas in the liquid path and measurement error can produce overlapping observations.
symptoms: Flow indication is below the site or process expectation
Reported process delivery is reduced or unstable
requiredContext: Pump manufacturer, exact model, impeller diameter/configuration and applicable curve revision
Driver type, actual speed or VFD frequency and operating mode
Fluid identity, temperature and relevant properties
Suction source level, suction piping arrangement and valve lineup
Discharge piping, control valve and downstream system state
Whether the condition is new, gradual, intermittent or linked to a recent change

hypotheses.cause: Suction-side restriction or inadequate source condition
supportingEvidence: Suction pressure loss or strainer differential pressure has changed relative to a comparable baseline at comparable flow
Source level or suction valve indication differs from the normal operating record
contradictingEvidence: Validated suction measurements and source conditions remain consistent with the applicable baseline at comparable operating conditions
confounders: Pressure tap location, plugged impulse line, faulty transmitter, changing flow or fluid temperature

hypotheses.cause: Discharge-side restriction or increased system resistance
supportingEvidence: Discharge pressure and system state differ from the documented operating baseline in a pattern consistent with increased resistance
Valve-position indication or downstream equipment state changed with the onset of low flow
contradictingEvidence: Discharge path and valve lineup are verified unchanged and pressure-flow behavior matches the expected system curve
confounders: Incorrect valve feedback, check-valve behavior, changing downstream demand or pressure instrument error

hypotheses.cause: Reduced actual pump speed or incorrect drive operating state
supportingEvidence: Measured or independently verified speed differs from the applicable normal operating state
VFD frequency or command history changed at the same time as the flow reduction
contradictingEvidence: Actual speed is independently verified and consistent with the correct pump curve and operating state
confounders: Command frequency is not proof of shaft speed; slip, coupling or feedback faults may matter

hypotheses.cause: Internal wear, excessive clearances or impeller damage
supportingEvidence: Performance has deteriorated progressively against a comparable baseline at verified speed and system conditions
Inspection after approved isolation identifies wear or damage
contradictingEvidence: Performance returns to expected behavior after correcting an external system or measurement issue
confounders: Fluid properties, impeller configuration, speed, system curve and measurement uncertainty

hypotheses.cause: Flow instrument, installation or signal-quality error
supportingEvidence: Flow indication conflicts with independent process observations or a suitable independent measurement
Instrument diagnostics, calibration history or signal quality indicate a possible fault
contradictingEvidence: Independent, suitable measurements confirm the low-flow condition under matching operating conditions
confounders: Different measurement technologies, installation requirements, averaging periods or non-steady operation

hypotheses.cause: Gas entrainment, air ingress or loss of prime where applicable
supportingEvidence: Unstable pressure/flow behavior coincides with evidence of gas ingress or loss of prime
The pump design and approved operating procedure make the suspected gas/prime mechanism applicable
contradictingEvidence: Pump is confirmed fully primed and the process fluid/installation provides no credible gas-ingress path
confounders: Pump type, venting arrangement, fluid vapor pressure, suction leak and sensor dynamics

measurements.name: Flow rate
measurements.location: Installed flowmeter; record tag and pipe location
measurements.operatingCondition: Stable operating point; record speed, valve state and fluid

measurements.name: Suction pressure
measurements.unit: kPa(g), bar(g) or absolute unit as installed
measurements.location: Identify exact suction pressure tap relative to pump datum
measurements.operatingCondition: Same timestamp as flow and discharge pressure where possible; record speed and fluid temperature

measurements.name: Discharge pressure
measurements.unit: kPa(g), bar(g) or absolute unit as installed
measurements.operatingCondition: Same timestamp as flow and suction pressure where possible; record downstream valve state

measurements.name: Pump speed
measurements.unit: rpm; VFD frequency in Hz is a separate field
measurements.location: Drive feedback or independent speed measurement; state which
measurements.operatingCondition: Record command, feedback and load state separately

measurements.name: Fluid temperature
measurements.operatingCondition: Record fluid identity and whether stable/transient

measurements.name: Strainer differential pressure
measurements.location: Across strainer, only if permanently instrumented
measurements.operatingCondition: Compare at comparable flow and fluid conditions

tests.name: Compare concurrent flow, suction pressure, discharge pressure and actual speed
prerequisites: Use existing installed instruments and approved HMI/historian read-only values
Confirm units, tag locations, timestamp alignment and instrument quality
Do not change valve positions or drive settings for this observation
expectedOutcomes: A coherent change in suction-side conditions redirects review toward source/suction hypotheses but does not prove a blockage
A verified speed change redirects review toward the drive/operating-state hypothesis
A flow indication inconsistent with independent evidence redirects review toward instrument validation
Pressure-flow behavior inconsistent with the applicable pump and system curves requires model/configuration review before cause ranking
interpretationLimits: A pressure value without tap location, unit, timestamp and operating condition is incomplete
PLC command/frequency is not equivalent to independently measured shaft speed
Do not use generic pressure or flow thresholds

tests.name: Review source level and installed valve-position indications
prerequisites: Read installed indicators from a safe location
Treat position feedback as an indication until independently verified
expectedOutcomes: A changed source level or suction lineup supports further review of suction availability
A changed discharge lineup or downstream state supports further review of system resistance
No recorded change leaves these hypotheses unresolved rather than disproved
interpretationLimits: A displayed valve position may not equal physical valve position
Do not manipulate valves as an experiment

tests.name: Plan physical inspection only after approved shutdown and isolation
prerequisites: Approved work order and site energy-control procedure
Verified isolation, depressurization, drainage and stored-energy controls
expectedOutcomes: Physical evidence of obstruction or damage supports the corresponding hypothesis within the inspected scope
No visible obstruction does not exclude hidden restrictions, incorrect clearances or intermittent process conditions
interpretationLimits: This is not an instruction to open equipment; use exact OEM and site procedures
Inspection findings must be recorded with component, location and photographs where permitted

limits: No universal numeric flow, pressure, vibration, current or temperature threshold is defined by this case
The exact pump curve, impeller, speed, fluid, datum, system curve and instrument installation govern interpretation
Do not infer cavitation solely from low flow, noise or one suction-pressure reading
Do not treat anomaly detection or a heuristic ranking as root-cause confirmation
Preserve measured, PLC-indicated, historian, estimated and unknown provenance separately
stopConditions: Unexpected severe vibration, abnormal noise, rapid temperature rise, visible hazardous leakage or an OEM/site stop alarm
Loss of prime or suspected dry running where the pump is not approved for that condition
Uncertain isolation, pressurized/hot/hazardous fluid exposure or need to remove a guard/open a line
Contradictory or implausible instrument values that cannot be safely validated
verification: Repeat flow, suction pressure, discharge pressure and speed measurements at a documented comparable operating point
Record the repaired or changed component and the exact intervention
Confirm stable operation against the correct OEM curve and site acceptance criteria
Keep the case unresolved if post-repair evidence is missing or operating conditions are not comparable

sources.claimScope: Research methods for selected seeded faults on one multistage pump test rig only; does not establish low-flow root-cause rules

limitations: The two registered open-access papers do not support the differential low-flow claims in this case
No exact-model OEM pump curve or primary source has yet been reviewed for this case
The case is candidate-only and must not be loaded into the live diagnosis ranking
Field validation and qualified technical review have not been performed
